1. [Maximum mark: 4]
The region $R$ is enclosed by the graph of $y=\mathrm{e}^{-x^2}$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=-1$ and $x=1$. Find the volume of the solid of revolution that is formed when $R$ is rotated through $2\pi$ about the $x$-axis.

2.text_clean:
2. [Maximum mark: 4]
The finishing times in a marathon race follow a normal distribution with mean $210$ minutes and standard deviation $22$ minutes.
(a) Find the probability that a runner finishes the race in under three hours. [2]
The fastest $90\%$ of the finishers receive a certificate.
(b) Find the time, below which a competitor has to complete the race, in order to gain a certificate. [2]

3.text_clean:
3. [Maximum mark: 5]
A mosaic is going to be created by randomly selecting $1000$ small tiles, each of which is either black or white. The probability that a tile is white is $0.1$. Let the random variable $W$ be the number of white tiles.
(a) State the distribution of $W$, including the values of any parameters. [2]
(b) Write down the mean of $W$. [1]
(c) Find $\mathrm{P}(W>89)$. [2]

4.text_clean:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]
A triangle ABC has $\hat{A}=50^\circ$, $\mathrm{AB}=7\text{ cm}$ and $\mathrm{BC}=6\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the triangle given that it is smaller than $10\text{ cm}^2$.

5.text_clean:
5. [Maximum mark: 5]
A bicycle inner tube can be considered as a joined up cylinder of fixed length $200\text{ cm}$ and radius $r\text{ cm}$. The radius $r$ increases as the inner tube is pumped up. Air is being pumped into the inner tube so that the volume of air in the tube increases at a constant rate of $30\text{ cm}^3\text{ s}^{-1}$. Find the rate at which the radius of the inner tube is increasing when $r=2\text{ cm}$.

6.text_clean:
6. [Maximum mark: 4]
A function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=x^3+\mathrm{e}^x+1$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$. By considering $f'(x)$ determine whether $f$ is a one-to-one or a many-to-one function.

7.text_clean:
7. [Maximum mark: 7]
The random variable $X$ follows a Poisson distribution with mean $m\neq 0$.
(a) Given that $2\mathrm{P}(X=4)=\mathrm{P}(X=5)$, show that $m=10$. [3]
(b) Given that $X\le 11$, find the probability that $X=6$. [4]

8. [Maximum mark: 8]
Let $\boldsymbol{v}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\5\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{w}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\\lambda\\10\end{pmatrix}$.
(a) Find the value of $\lambda$ for $\boldsymbol{v}$ and $\boldsymbol{w}$ to be parallel. [2]
(b) Find the value of $\lambda$ for $\boldsymbol{v}$ and $\boldsymbol{w}$ to be perpendicular. [2]
(c) Find the two values of $\lambda$ if the angle between $\boldsymbol{v}$ and $\boldsymbol{w}$ is $10^\circ$. [4]

9.text_clean:
9. [Maximum mark: 7]
Find the equation of the normal to the curve $y=\dfrac{\mathrm{e}^x\cos x\ln(x+\mathrm{e})}{\left(x^{17}+1\right)^5}$ at the point where $x=0$.
In your answer give the value of the gradient, of the normal, to three decimal places.

10. [Maximum mark: 10]
A function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=(x+1)(x-1)(x-5)$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
(a) Find the values of $x$ for which $f(x)<|f(x)|$. [3]
A function $g$ is defined by $g(x)=x^2+x-6$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$.
(b) Find the values of $x$ for which $g(x)<\dfrac{1}{g(x)}$. [7]

11.text_clean:
11. [Maximum mark: 20]
The probability density function of a continuous random variable $X$ is given by
$f(x)=\begin{cases}0, & x<0\\ \dfrac{\sin x}{4}, & 0\le x\le\pi\\ a(x-\pi), & \pi<x\le 2\pi\\ 0, & 2\pi<x\end{cases}$.
(a) Sketch the graph of $y=f(x)$. [2]
(b) Find $\mathrm{P}(X\le\pi)$. [2]
(c) Show that $a=\dfrac{1}{\pi^2}$. [3]
(d) Write down the median of $X$. [1]
(e) Calculate the mean of $X$. [3]
(f) Calculate the variance of $X$. [3]
(g) Find $\mathrm{P}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\le X\le\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$. [2]
(h) Given that $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\le X\le\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ find the probability that $\pi\le X\le 2\pi$. [4]

12.text_clean:
12. [Maximum mark: 19]
(a) (i) Use the binomial theorem to expand $(\cos\theta+\mathrm{i}\sin\theta)^5$.
(ii) Hence use De Moivre's theorem to prove $\sin 5\theta=5\cos^4\theta\sin\theta-10\cos^2\theta\sin^3\theta+\sin^5\theta$.
(iii) State a similar expression for $\cos 5\theta$ in terms of $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$. [6]
Let $z=r(\cos\alpha+\mathrm{i}\sin\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is measured in degrees, be the solution of $z^5-1=0$ which has the smallest positive argument.
(b) Find the value of $r$ and the value of $\alpha$. [4]
(c) Using (a) (ii) and your answer from (b) show that $16\sin^4\alpha-20\sin^2\alpha+5=0$. [4]
(d) Hence express $\sin 72^\circ$ in the form $\dfrac{\sqrt{a+b\sqrt{c}}}{d}$ where $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{Z}$. [5]

13.text_clean:
13. [Maximum mark: 21]
Richard, a marine soldier, steps out of a stationary helicopter, $1000\text{ m}$ above the ground, at time $t=0$. Let his height, in metres, above the ground be given by $s(t)$. For the first $10$ seconds his velocity, $v(t)\text{ m s}^{-1}$, is given by $v(t)=-10t$.
(a) (i) Find his acceleration $a(t)$ for $t<10$.
(ii) Calculate $v(10)$.
(iii) Show that $s(10)=500$. [6]
At $t=10$ his parachute opens and his acceleration $a(t)$ is subsequently given by $a(t)=-10-5v$, $t\ge 10$.
(b) Given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}v}=\dfrac{1}{\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}t}}$, write down $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}v}$ in terms of $v$. [1]
You are told that Richard's acceleration, $a(t)=-10-5v$, is always positive, for $t\ge 10$.
(c) Hence show that $t=10+\dfrac{1}{5}\ln\left(\dfrac{98}{-2-v}\right)$. [5]
(d) Hence find an expression for the velocity, $v$, for $t\ge 10$. [2]
(e) Find an expression for his height, $s$, above the ground for $t\ge 10$. [5]
(f) Find the value of $t$ when Richard lands on the ground. [2]
